page: Amazon Web Services c8g.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors built on the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture. It features 64 dedicated physical cores and 64 vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz, with a single thread per core configuration. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and includes a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the c8g.16xlarge exhibits top-tier multi-core and memory performance. Its memory subsystem achieves top-tier read-only cached bandwidth of 7394.89 GB/sec and uncached read bandwidth of 459.06 GB/sec. Multi-core processing capabilities are highlighted by top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core, software compilation with Clang, and Passmark CPU physics tests. Database operations and Redis SET benchmarks also rank in the top tier, with Redis handling 131.06 million operations per second. Single-core performance, however, remains in the average tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ARMv9 architecture delivers high multi-threaded resource density and memory bandwidth without the overhead of hyperthreading, making it highly efficient for parallelized workloads. The instance is well-suited for compute-intensive workloads such as software compilation, high-throughput static web serving, database operations, and multi-threaded data decompression.
